headline: Medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks arise from ChatGPT Desktop’s file/clipboard/screen inputs feeding PaddleOCR’s document parsing.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest uploaded files, clipboard, screenshots, and files from supported macOS apps, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images. If OCR output or extracted text is copied into ChatGPT, malicious document content can steer downstream instructions. The pair has a plausible shared-content bridge, though not a documented direct channel.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is pasted or imported into ChatGPT Desktop without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF the shared content includes attacker-controlled document text or screenshots, ChatGPT may treat it as instructions.
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/template when pasting OCR output into ChatGPT.
Strip instructions from OCR text before forwarding it.
Review only a small excerpt first to detect instruction-like content.
Disable clipboard-based transfer for untrusted documents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between OCR and chat inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, and sends requests to api.openai.com; PaddleOCR handles documents/images with allowlisted egress. If sensitive documents are OCR’d and then forwarded into ChatGPT, both agents can expose the same data class across separate backends. The shared-workflow leakage path is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are processed by PaddleOCR and then copied into ChatGPT Desktop, the same content leaves the local workflow twice.
IF the documents contain regulated or confidential data, leakage impact increases.
mitigations: Avoid sending sensitive OCR outputs to ChatGPT.
Redact identifiers before any handoff.
Process only non-sensitive samples in the pair.
Confirm both tools are using approved data classes only.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before cross-tool transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read-only filesystem access and no write, git, shell, or MCP capabilities; PaddleOCR exposes browser use and allowlisted egress but no filesystem write or git state. Overlapping write authority is absent, so direct resource conflict is limited to read-side contention or user-managed files.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would rise.
IF the user manually synchronizes mutable files between them, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Keep shared folders read-only.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same document.
Use separate working copies.
Check file timestamps before overwriting.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce extracted facts from files/screenshots, and PaddleOCR can consume documents/images for downstream parsing. If one agent’s output is forwarded into the other without verification, OCR or chat hallucinations can cascade into incorrect summaries or actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles.
conditions: IF ChatGPT-generated text is treated as authoritative input to PaddleOCR workflows, errors can propagate.
IF PaddleOCR output is reused by ChatGPT without human verification, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between tools.
Cross-check key facts against the original document.
Use confidence thresholds before forwarding outputs.
Limit automation to non-critical drafts.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between extraction and generation.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not declare PHI, GDPR, or residency commitments, so a specific compliance breach is not proven. However, ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while PaddleOCR handles documents/images; if regulated data is routed through both, policy mismatch could arise. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent residency issue.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed through both tools, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency policies differ between the two services, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict the pair to non-regulated data.
Check vendor retention settings before use.
Document approved data classes for each tool.
Avoid cross-border transfer of sensitive documents.
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing agreement and residency controls.
